subject: ParcelX: allocator split -> degraded throughput & proposed remediation
messages:

Date: 2029-09-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: Degraded inference throughput for ParcelX — urgent

Ben —

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and slow responses against our dedicated pool in us-west around 08:02 PDT (trace IDs: px-7f9a, px-7f9b). Latency for our highest-QPS endpoints spiked from ~70ms to >1.8s, and roughly 18% of calls returned 503s over a 12-minute window. This is impacting our checkout personalization flows.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and whether you have an estimated time to recovery? We have an internal ops page showing sustained queue depth and call failures. Please escalate — our SREs are standing by.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@parcelx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-09-05T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Degraded inference throughput for ParcelX — urgent

Emma — thanks for the heads up and the capture. We see the same symptom in our monitoring and have opened RW-9876 for tracking. Short update:

- What happened: around 08:00 PDT an internal network fabric partition affected the us-west reserved pool. The partition caused an allocator split where nodes on one side stopped accepting rebalancing requests. That prevented our continuous balancer from draining hot nodes, which increased queue depth and produced 5xx throttles on affected tenants.
- Immediate mitigation we applied: we routed ParcelX traffic to the standby subset inside your reserved pool and enabled short-lived burst capacity for 20 minutes to clear the backlog. That cut 5xx to <1% and reduced 99th latency toward normal.
- Next steps: our reliability team is running a targeted repair to heal the fabric and reconcile the allocator. I expect a full cluster rebalance in the next 2–4 hours. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and a proposed runbook change.

I've looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Naomi (TAM) to coordinate credits and a postmortem. Connor O'Brien on reliability is triaging the allocator logs now.

Please share any additional traces and we'd like to set a 30-minute catch-up within the next 24 hours to review impact and RTO expectations.

—Ben

>

Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com> replied:

> Quick summary from the reliability side (logs attached):
> - At 07:59:34 PDT we observed a split brain condition across fabric-group-3. Heartbeats from a subset of nodes stopped being processed by the allocator master because of transient packet drops between top-of-rack switches.
> - The allocator continued to mark nodes as healthy due to stale liveness windows while the balancer couldn't establish leases on the affected set. This left hot shards pinned to isolated nodes.
> - We attempted an automated rebalance at 08:05 PDT but the controller aborted because it couldn't confirm shard leases across both halves.
> - Manual repair (force-resume and targeted lease reconciliation) was initiated at 08:22 PDT, followed by staged drain on the isolated nodes. By 08:42 PDT queue depth returned to normal ranges.
> 
> Immediate fixes proposed: increase liveness frequency under spotty fabric conditions, add a fabric partition detector to trigger an emergency rebalance, and introduce a conservative fallback routing policy that will temporarily switch affected tenants to standby replicas automatically.
> 
> Attaching: support_log_excerpt.txt (filtered allocator and balancer logs).

Connor
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@parcelx.com>, ops@parcelx.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-09-06T18:15:00Z
Subject: ParcelX — incident update, remediation completed, and next steps

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for flagging this and for your patience. I wanted to summarize where we are and our proposed follow-ups: 

What we confirmed
- Root cause: transient network fabric packet drops caused an allocator split in the us-west reserved pool which blocked automated balancer progress. That produced transient queue pileups and a window of elevated 5xxs (peak ~18% over 12 minutes).
- Impact window: 2029-09-05 07:59:00–08:12:00 PDT (primary impact), with residual latency settling by 08:42 PDT after manual intervention.

Actions taken
- Immediate: traffic routed to standby subset, temporary burst capacity enabled to clear backlog (08:12–08:32 PDT).
- Repair: manual lease reconciliation and staged drain of isolated nodes, followed by a full cluster rebalance.
- Preventive: applied a conservative change to liveness checks in the affected cluster and created a fabric-partition detector to fail over earlier if packet drops exceed threshold.

Proposed customer-facing items
- Postmortem: we will deliver a detailed postmortem doc (initial draft attached) within 72 hours, including logs and timeline.
- Runbook changes: we propose a runbook edit that adds an automatic fallback to standby replicas for reserved pools when a fabric partition is detected. Draft attached: runbook-change-proposal.md
- Credit: we propose a one-time service credit equivalent to 25% of affected 12-minute usage for the impacted interval; Naomi can coordinate exact dollar calculation if you want to take that route.

Requested next steps
1) Can we schedule a 30-minute review with your SREs tomorrow (09/07) at 10:00 PDT? If that doesn't work, propose a time.
2) Please let Naomi know if ParcelX prefers a credit or an invoice-level adjustment.
3) Any additional traces you can share will help us finalize the timeline appendix.

Attachments: support_log_excerpt.txt (filtered), postmortem-draft.docx, runbook-change-proposal.md

Thanks — we take this seriously and are prioritizing changes to avoid recurrence.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
